newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cement firm to privatise at least 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cement firm to privatise at least 10 pct.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries said on Friday it would sell to anchor investors at least 2.5 million shares, or 10 percent, of its Helwan Portland Cement.
Individuals, mutual funds and financial institutions are currently hold 29.8 percent of Helwan Cement. The holding company holds the remaining 70.2 percent.
The partial privatisation, whose agents are Misr Exterior Bank and EFG-Hermes securities group, is to be executed through auction, the parent company said. Details will be announced shortly.
Helwan Cement increased net profits for financial year 1995/96 by 21 percent to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million a year earlier. The financial year ended on June 30.
Net profits in the first quarter of 96/97 were 35 million pounds.

The firm, one of Egypt's leading cement manufacturers, raised dividends for 1995/96 to five pounds from the 4.75 pounds it had promised investors earlier this year. Dividends for 1994/95 were four pounds per share.
The firm's net sales rose to 545 million pounds from 487 million in 1994/95.
It owns 7.19 percent of the partly private Suez Cement, one of Egypt's best performing cement companies.
